entities.name: Mycetoma
entities.description: A chronic, progressively destructive, indolent granulomatous inflammatory disease of subcutaneous tissues, skin, and underlying bone, endemic within the tropical and subtropical Mycetoma Belt, caused by true filamentous fungi (eumycetoma) or aerobic actinomycete bacteria (actinomycetoma).

entities.name: Minor Percutaneous Traumatic Inoculation via Acacia Thorns While Walking Barefoot
entities.description: Direct mechanical inoculation of soil-dwelling organisms through broken skin via penetrating trauma from acacia tree thorns (Acacia nilotica), dry plant splinters, wood chips, or sharp stones in individuals walking barefoot.

entities.name: Arid and Semi-Arid Geographic Endemicity in the Mycetoma Belt
entities.description: Residence or prolonged travel within the hyperendemic tropical and subtropical 'Mycetoma Belt' between latitudes 15°S and 30°N (notably Sudan, Mexico, India, Mauritania, Somalia, Senegal, Chad, Ethiopia, and Yemen) characterized by low rainfall and thorny scrub vegetation.

entities.name: High-Risk Agricultural or Pastoralist Occupation Without Protective Footwear
entities.description: Employment in rural subsistence agriculture, field labor, or nomadic livestock pastoralism without protective footwear or gloves, conferring high occupational risk of percutaneous micro-trauma and soil contact.

entities.name: Carrying Contaminated Firewood, Crops, or Soil-Laden Sacks on Back or Shoulders
entities.description: Manual carrying of thorny acacia branches, dry firewood, agricultural crops, or soil-laden sacks directly on the shoulders or back, resulting in upper trunk and extra-pedal inoculation.

entities.name: Madurella mycetomatis
entities.description: The predominant causative fungal agent of black-grain eumycetoma globally (>70% of eumycetoma cases), forming dark melanized cement-embedded grains with thick-walled hyphae and chlamydoconidia, hyperendemic in Sudan and Africa.

entities.name: Trematosphaeria grisea
entities.description: A dematiaceous filamentous fungal pathogen (formerly Madurella grisea) causing black-grain eumycetoma with tubular or hollow pigmented grains.

entities.name: Falciformispora senegalensis
entities.description: An ascomycete fungus (formerly Leptosphaeria senegalensis) causing black-grain eumycetoma characterized by dark granules containing large vesicular swollen cells.

entities.name: Scedosporium boydii
entities.description: A hyaline filamentous mold belonging to the Pseudallescheria boydii species complex, causing white-to-yellow grain eumycetoma with slender septate hyphae.

entities.name: Acremonium falciforme
entities.description: A hyaline filamentous fungus causing white-to-yellowish grain eumycetoma with delicate hyphae.

entities.name: Nocardia brasiliensis
entities.description: An aerobic, branching, partially acid-fast Gram-positive actinomycete bacterium producing small white-to-yellow grains; the leading cause of actinomycetoma in Mexico and Central/South America.

entities.name: Actinomadura madurae
entities.description: An aerobic actinomycete bacterium causing actinomycetoma characterized by large, soft white, cream-colored, or yellowish-to-pink grains, distributed worldwide.

entities.name: Streptomyces somaliensis
entities.description: An aerobic actinomycete bacterium causing yellow-to-brown grain actinomycetoma characterized by dense, hard, cement-bound grains, prevalent in arid regions of Sudan and the Horn of Africa.

entities.name: Actinomadura pelletieri
entities.description: An aerobic actinomycete bacterium producing distinctive small, hard, brilliant crimson or bright red grains and causing aggressive, rapidly destructive osteolytic actinomycetoma.

entities.name: Nocardia asteroides
entities.description: An aerobic, partially acid-fast branching Gram-positive bacterium capable of producing white-to-yellowish microcolonies and actinomycetoma.

entities.name: Classic Triad of Painless Subcutaneous Mass Multiple Sinus Tracts and Grain Discharge
entities.description: The pathognomonic clinical hallmark triad of mycetoma consisting of a firm indolent subcutaneous mass (tumefaction), multiple interconnected cutaneous sinus openings, and active discharge containing macroscopic pigmented grains.

entities.name: Firm Indurated Painless Subcutaneous Tumefaction with Deep Fascial Fixation
entities.description: A woody, non-tender, slow-growing subcutaneous nodule or indurated mass bound to underlying muscle fascial planes and deep structures, typically on the foot ('Madura foot') or lower extremity.

entities.name: Multiple Elevated Crater-Like Interconnected Cutaneous Sinus Tracts
entities.description: Multiple raised, crateriform cutaneous fistulous openings adhering to deep intermuscular fascial planes and draining serosanguinous, purulent, or oily fluid.

entities.name: Macroscopic Black Grains Discharging from Cutaneous Sinuses
entities.description: Visible, discrete, hard pigmented microcolonies (0.5 to 2 mm) ranging from dark brown to coal-black, pathognomonic of fungal eumycetoma caused by Madurella species or Trematosphaeria grisea.

entities.name: Macroscopic Bright Red Grains Discharging from Cutaneous Sinuses
entities.description: Visible, small, hard, brilliant deep red or garnet-colored microcolonies (0.3 to 0.5 mm), pathognomonic of bacterial actinomycetoma caused by Actinomadura pelletieri.

entities.name: Macroscopic White to Yellow Grains Discharging from Cutaneous Sinuses
entities.description: Visible soft or firm pale yellowish-white microcolonies (0.5 to 2 mm) observed in discharge, indicative of either bacterial actinomycetoma (Actinomadura madurae, Nocardia brasiliensis) or fungal eumycetoma (Scedosporium boydii).

entities.name: Striking Absence of Pain and Fever Despite Massive Deforming Tissue Swelling
entities.description: Indolent clinical presentation in >85% of patients with normal body temperature and absent local tenderness despite massive limb deformity and extensive osteolysis, mediated by anesthetic fungal/bacterial metabolic products.

entities.name: Direct Microscopic Examination of Grains via 10-20% KOH Mount and Gram Stain
entities.description: Direct bedside microscopic examination of crushed grain discharge revealing either thick, septate, branched fungal hyphae (2-6 um) with chlamydoconidia in dark cement matrix (eumycetoma) or delicate Gram-positive branching bacterial filaments (<1 um) and cocci (actinomycetoma).

entities.name: Modified Kinyoun Acid-Fast Staining Demonstrating Partially Acid-Fast Branching Filaments
entities.description: Direct cytological acid-fast stain on crushed pale grains demonstrating partially acid-fast branching filaments, confirming Nocardia species infection.

entities.name: Dot-in-Circle Sign on T2-Weighted and Contrast-Enhanced MRI
entities.description: Pathognomonic magnetic resonance imaging feature on T2-weighted and contrast sequences featuring round, high-signal granulomatous spheres containing a central or eccentric low-signal punctate dot representing the grain.

entities.name: Point-of-Care Ultrasound Demonstrating Thick-Walled Hypoechoic Granulomas with Hyper-Reflective Central Echoes
entities.description: Musculoskeletal ultrasound showing multiple thick-walled hypoechoic cavities containing sharp hyper-reflective central echoes with acoustic shadowing corresponding to fungal grains in eumycetoma.

entities.name: Plain Radiography Showing Multiple Punched-Out Osteolytic Cavities with Preserved Joint Spaces
entities.description: Plain limb radiograph demonstrating extensive soft-tissue lobulation, periosteal cortical reaction, and round punched-out osteolytic bone cavities ('geodes' or 'moth-eaten' appearance) characteristically preserving articular joint spaces until end-stage destruction.

entities.name: Chronic Inflammatory Blood Profile with Markedly Elevated ESR and Normal White Blood Cell Count
entities.description: Admission laboratory evaluation demonstrating moderately to markedly elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (40-80 mm/h) in the presence of normal leukocyte counts and absent acute leukocytosis, indicative of chronic indolent granulomatous inflammation.

entities.name: Acute Rapidly Progressive Inflammatory Swelling Developing Within Less Than 4 Weeks
entities.description: Sudden onset of painful, hot, erythematous limb swelling evolving within days to under 4 weeks rules out uncomplicated primary mycetoma, which characteristically evolves over months to years (mean 2-5 years).

entities.name: Complete Absence of Discharging Macroscopic Grains or Granules from Active Sinuses
entities.description: Exudate or aspirate from chronic draining sinuses that consistently lacks macroscopic or microscopic colored grains or microcolonies rules out active typical mycetoma.

entities.name: Rapid Systemic Pyogenic Sepsis with High Fever and Prominent Neutrophilic Leukocytosis at Initial Presentation
entities.description: Acute presentation characterized by spiking fevers, chills, toxic hemodynamics, and high neutrophilic leukocytosis at initial presentation rules out uncomplicated mycetoma, pointing toward acute pyogenic bacterial cellulitis or acute osteomyelitis.

entities.name: Presence of Pigmented Medlar Bodies Copper Pennies on Cytological Examination
entities.description: Cytological or histological visualization of thick-walled, golden-brown muriform cells ('medlar bodies' or 'copper pennies') on microscopic scraping rules out mycetoma and establishes the diagnosis of chromoblastomycosis.

entities.name: Chronic Pyogenic Bacterial Osteomyelitis
entities.description: A pyogenic bacterial bone infection (predominantly Staphylococcus aureus) characterized by severe localized bone pain, fevers, acute leukocytosis, and purulent sinus discharge lacking discrete colored grains.

entities.name: Osteosarcoma
entities.description: A primary malignant bone tumor presenting with a rapidly growing, painful extremity mass and aggressive cortical bone destruction with periosteal reaction, but lacking cutaneous sinuses, fistulae, or grain discharge.

entities.name: Chromoblastomycosis
entities.description: A chronic subcutaneous fungal infection presenting as superficial, cauliflower-like, verrucous hyperkeratotic plaques with surface black dots and pathognomonic medlar bodies, lacking deep bone geodes, deep sinus tracts, or grain discharge.

entities.name: Podoconiosis
entities.description: An endemic non-filarial geochemical elephantiasis caused by barefoot exposure to volcanic red clay soils, presenting as ascending bilateral non-pitting lymphedema, hyperkeratosis, and mossy papillomas without sinus tracts, bone cavities, or grains.

entities.name: Lymphatic Filariasis
entities.description: A mosquito-borne parasitic nematode disease (Wuchereria bancrofti) presenting with hydrocele and chronic ascending lymphatic elephantiasis, lacking localized crater-like sinus tracts, bone geodes, or grain discharge.

entities.name: Kaposi Sarcoma
entities.description: A vascular neoplasm associated with HHV-8 causing multiple violaceous cutaneous plaques, nodules, and lymphedema of the lower extremities, lacking sinus tracts, osteolytic cavitations, and grain discharge.

entities.name: The Welsh Regimen of Amikacin Cycles Combined with Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole
entities.description: Chemotherapy protocol for actinomycetoma consisting of pulse amikacin (15 mg/kg/day for 3-week cycles) combined with oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX 800/160 mg twice daily for 6-12 months), achieving medical cure in >90% of cases without surgery.

entities.name: Oral Itraconazole Chemotherapy Combined with Wide Surgical Excision
entities.description: Standard curative protocol for eumycetoma consisting of pre-operative oral itraconazole (200 mg twice daily for 6-12 months) to encapsulate the lesion, followed by wide local surgical excision, and post-operative continuation of itraconazole.

entities.name: Oral Voriconazole Second-Line Chemotherapy
entities.description: Second-line expanded-spectrum oral triazole antifungal therapy (200 mg twice daily) effective in refractory eumycetoma or cases caused by Scedosporium boydii.

entities.name: Primary Surgical Excision Alone Without Antifungal Coverage in Eumycetoma
entities.description: Incomplete or primary surgical excision performed without prolonged preoperative and postoperative antifungal coverage, resulting in catastrophic high rates of local recurrence and deep fascial dissemination.

entities.name: Standard Antibacterial Therapy Administered for Fungal Eumycetoma
entities.description: Administration of antibacterial agents (such as the Welsh regimen or beta-lactam antibiotics) for fungal eumycetoma, which yields zero therapeutic efficacy and leads to uncontrolled disease progression and limb loss.

entities.name: Antifungal Azole Monotherapy Administered for Bacterial Actinomycetoma
entities.description: Administration of antifungal azole agents (itraconazole, ketoconazole, voriconazole) for bacterial actinomycetoma, which has no antibacterial activity and results in treatment failure.

relationships.target: Minor Percutaneous Traumatic Inoculation via Acacia Thorns While Walking Barefoot
relationships.keywords: percutaneous inoculation, trauma, acacia thorns, barefoot walking, transmission
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Mycetoma is acquired through percutaneous traumatic inoculation of soil-dwelling fungi or bacteria via acacia tree thorns, plant splinters, or sharp stones in barefoot individuals.

relationships.target: Arid and Semi-Arid Geographic Endemicity in the Mycetoma Belt
relationships.keywords: geographic distribution, mycetoma belt, arid climate, endemicity
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma hyperendemicity is concentrated within the arid and semi-arid 'Mycetoma Belt' between latitudes 15°S and 30°N with sparse rainfall and thorny scrub vegetation.

relationships.target: High-Risk Agricultural or Pastoralist Occupation Without Protective Footwear
relationships.keywords: occupational exposure, farmers, herdsmen, agricultural labor
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma predominantly affects barefoot rural agricultural workers, manual field laborers, and nomadic pastoralists.

relationships.target: Carrying Contaminated Firewood, Crops, or Soil-Laden Sacks on Back or Shoulders
relationships.keywords: occupational carrying, firewood trauma, upper trunk mycetoma, shoulder lesion
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Carrying thorny firewood, dry brush, or soil-contaminated crop sacks on the shoulders or back provides a direct percutaneous exposure route resulting in extra-pedal trunk mycetoma.

relationships.target: Madurella mycetomatis
relationships.keywords: fungal pathogen, eumycetoma, black grains, Sudan
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Madurella mycetomatis is the primary causative fungal pathogen of black-grain eumycetoma, accounting for more than 70% of eumycetoma cases globally.

relationships.target: Trematosphaeria grisea
relationships.keywords: dematiaceous fungus, eumycetoma, black grains
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Trematosphaeria grisea is an etiologic dematiaceous fungus causing black-grain eumycetoma.

relationships.target: Falciformispora senegalensis
relationships.keywords: fungal pathogen, ascomycete, black grains, eumycetoma
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Falciformispora senegalensis is an ascomycete fungal pathogen responsible for black-grain eumycetoma.

relationships.target: Scedosporium boydii
relationships.keywords: hyaline mold, white grains, yellow grains, eumycetoma
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Scedosporium boydii is a filamentous hyaline fungal mold that causes pale white-to-yellow grain eumycetoma.

relationships.target: Acremonium falciforme
relationships.keywords: fungal pathogen, pale grains, eumycetoma
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Acremonium falciforme is an etiologic hyaline fungal species that causes white-to-yellow grain eumycetoma.

relationships.target: Nocardia brasiliensis
relationships.keywords: actinomycete, bacterial pathogen, actinomycetoma, Mexico
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Nocardia brasiliensis is an aerobic, partially acid-fast actinomycete bacterium causing actinomycetoma with small white-to-yellow grains, highly prevalent in the Americas.

relationships.target: Actinomadura madurae
relationships.keywords: actinomycete, bacterial pathogen, actinomycetoma, pale grains
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Actinomadura madurae is an aerobic branching actinomycete bacterium causing actinomycetoma characterized by large white-to-yellow or pink grains.

relationships.target: Streptomyces somaliensis
relationships.keywords: actinomycete, bacterial pathogen, yellow grains, actinomycetoma
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Streptomyces somaliensis is an aerobic actinomycete bacterium causing yellow-to-brown grain actinomycetoma in arid regions.

relationships.target: Actinomadura pelletieri
relationships.keywords: actinomycete, red grains, aggressive actinomycetoma
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Actinomadura pelletieri is an aerobic actinomycete bacterium producing pathognomonic small, bright red grains and aggressive osteolytic lesions.

relationships.target: Nocardia asteroides
relationships.keywords: actinomycete, bacterial pathogen, actinomycetoma
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Nocardia asteroides is an aerobic branching bacterium recognized as a causative agent of actinomycetoma.

relationships.target: Classic Triad of Painless Subcutaneous Mass Multiple Sinus Tracts and Grain Discharge
relationships.keywords: pathognomonic hallmark, cardinal triad, tumefaction, sinuses, grain discharge
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] The physical triad of painless subcutaneous tumefaction, multiple discharging cutaneous sinuses, and macroscopic grains is the cardinal clinical hallmark of mycetoma.

relationships.target: Firm Indurated Painless Subcutaneous Tumefaction with Deep Fascial Fixation
relationships.keywords: tumefaction, nodule, woody induration, madura foot
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Mycetoma presents as an indolent, woody, firm, non-tender subcutaneous mass bound to deep fascial planes.

relationships.target: Multiple Elevated Crater-Like Interconnected Cutaneous Sinus Tracts
relationships.keywords: sinus tracts, fistulae, draining openings, fascial planes
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Mycetoma develops multiple crater-like discharging sinus tracts interconnected across intermuscular fascial planes.

relationships.target: Macroscopic Black Grains Discharging from Cutaneous Sinuses
relationships.keywords: black grains, eumycetoma, pathognomonic sign, Madurella
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Discharging macroscopic black grains (0.5 to 2 mm) are pathognomonic of fungal eumycetoma, predominantly caused by Madurella mycetomatis.

relationships.target: Macroscopic Bright Red Grains Discharging from Cutaneous Sinuses
relationships.keywords: red grains, Actinomadura pelletieri, pathognomonic sign, actinomycetoma
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Discharging macroscopic bright red grains are pathognomonic of bacterial actinomycetoma caused by Actinomadura pelletieri.

relationships.target: Macroscopic White to Yellow Grains Discharging from Cutaneous Sinuses
relationships.keywords: pale grains, yellow grains, actinomycetoma, Scedosporium, Nocardia
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Discharging pale white-to-yellow grains indicate either bacterial actinomycetoma (Actinomadura madurae, Nocardia brasiliensis) or fungal eumycetoma (Scedosporium boydii).

relationships.target: Striking Absence of Pain and Fever Despite Massive Deforming Tissue Swelling
relationships.keywords: indolent swelling, afebrile presentation, lack of pain, deforming mass
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Mycetoma lesions remain non-tender and patients remain afebrile in >85% of cases despite grotesque limb deformity and bone invasion.

relationships.target: Direct Microscopic Examination of Grains via 10-20% KOH Mount and Gram Stain
relationships.keywords: direct microscopy, KOH mount, Gram stain, fungal hyphae, bacterial filaments
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Direct grain cytology rapidly differentiates broad branched septate fungal hyphae (eumycetoma) from delicate Gram-positive branching bacterial filaments (actinomycetoma).

relationships.target: Modified Kinyoun Acid-Fast Staining Demonstrating Partially Acid-Fast Branching Filaments
relationships.keywords: modified Kinyoun, acid-fast stain, Nocardia identification
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Modified Kinyoun acid-fast staining identifies delicate partially acid-fast branching bacterial filaments diagnostic of Nocardia species.

relationships.target: Dot-in-Circle Sign on T2-Weighted and Contrast-Enhanced MRI
relationships.keywords: MRI, dot-in-circle sign, pathognomonic imaging, granuloma
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrates the pathognomonic dot-in-circle sign on T2-weighted scans, showing high-signal granulomatous spheres surrounding low-signal grain dots.

relationships.target: Point-of-Care Ultrasound Demonstrating Thick-Walled Hypoechoic Granulomas with Hyper-Reflective Central Echoes
relationships.keywords: ultrasound, POCUS, hyper-reflective echoes, acoustic shadowing, grains
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Point-of-care ultrasound demonstrates thick-walled hypoechoic granulomas containing bright central hyper-reflective echoes with acoustic shadowing corresponding to grains.

relationships.target: Plain Radiography Showing Multiple Punched-Out Osteolytic Cavities with Preserved Joint Spaces
relationships.keywords: plain X-ray, osteolytic cavities, geodes, moth-eaten bone, joint preservation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Plain radiography displays soft-tissue swelling, periosteal cortical reaction, and round punched-out osteolytic bone cavities ('geodes') with preserved articular spaces until late disease.

relationships.target: Chronic Inflammatory Blood Profile with Markedly Elevated ESR and Normal White Blood Cell Count
relationships.keywords: elevated ESR, normal WBC, chronic inflammation, absence of leukocytosis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission laboratory testing reveals moderate-to-severe ESR elevation (40-80 mm/h) with normal total leukocyte counts and absent neutrophilia.

relationships.target: Acute Rapidly Progressive Inflammatory Swelling Developing Within Less Than 4 Weeks
relationships.keywords: acute onset, rapid swelling, exclusion criteria, cellulitis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Acute localized pain, erythema, and rapid volumetric swelling developing in less than 4 weeks rules out primary mycetoma, which progresses insidiously over months to years.

relationships.target: Complete Absence of Discharging Macroscopic Grains or Granules from Active Sinuses
relationships.keywords: absence of grains, negative exudate, rule out mycetoma
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Persistent absence of macroscopic or microscopic grains upon careful inspection of discharge or deep aspirate rules out active typical mycetoma.

relationships.target: Rapid Systemic Pyogenic Sepsis with High Fever and Prominent Neutrophilic Leukocytosis at Initial Presentation
relationships.keywords: systemic sepsis, high fever, leukocytosis, acute bacterial infection
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Acute presentation with spiking fevers, chills, toxic hemodynamics, and high neutrophilic leukocytosis at initial presentation rules out uncomplicated mycetoma.

relationships.target: Presence of Pigmented Medlar Bodies Copper Pennies on Cytological Examination
relationships.keywords: medlar bodies, copper pennies, muriform cells, chromoblastomycosis exclusion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Identification of golden-brown muriform cells ('medlar bodies' or 'copper pennies') on direct microscopic scraping rules out mycetoma and confirms chromoblastomycosis.

relationships.target: Chronic Pyogenic Bacterial Osteomyelitis
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, osteomyelitis, bone pain, fever, Staphylococcus aureus
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Chronic pyogenic osteomyelitis presents with severe bone pain, systemic fevers, acute neutrophilic leukocytosis, and sinus discharge without colored grains, unlike indolent, painless mycetoma.

relationships.target: Osteosarcoma
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, osteosarcoma, bone neoplasm, periosteal reaction
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Osteosarcoma causes painful rapidly expanding bone tumefaction and aggressive periosteal reactions without draining sinuses, fistulae, or grain discharge.

relationships.target: Chromoblastomycosis
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, chromoblastomycosis, verrucous plaques, medlar bodies
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Chromoblastomycosis produces superficial, cauliflower-like verrucous plaques with black surface dots and diagnostic medlar bodies, lacking deep sinus tracts, bone cavities, or grain discharge.

relationships.target: Podoconiosis
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, podoconiosis, endemic elephantiasis, lymphedema
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Podoconiosis produces bilateral ascending non-pitting lymphedema and mossy skin changes without cutaneous sinus openings, osteolytic geodes, or grain discharge.

relationships.target: Lymphatic Filariasis
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, lymphatic filariasis, elephantiasis, Wuchereria
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Lymphatic filariasis presents with chronic lymphatic obstruction and elephantiasis without localized discharging sinus tracts, bone destruction, or grain shedding.

relationships.target: Kaposi Sarcoma
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, Kaposi sarcoma, violaceous plaques, HHV-8
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Kaposi sarcoma manifests as violaceous vascular plaques and nodular lesions with lymphedema, lacking deep sinus tracts, bone geodes, and grain discharge.

relationships.target: The Welsh Regimen of Amikacin Cycles Combined with Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole
relationships.keywords: Welsh regimen, amikacin, TMP-SMX, actinomycetoma cure, medical therapy
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Actinomycetoma achieves complete cure in >90% of cases using cyclical amikacin combined with oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (Welsh regimen) without surgical resection.

relationships.target: Oral Itraconazole Chemotherapy Combined with Wide Surgical Excision
relationships.keywords: itraconazole, wide surgical excision, eumycetoma cure, combined therapy
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Eumycetoma responds to long-term oral itraconazole (6-12 months) combined with meticulous wide local surgical excision.

relationships.target: Oral Voriconazole Second-Line Chemotherapy
relationships.keywords: voriconazole, second-line antifungal, refractory eumycetoma, Scedosporium
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Eumycetoma refractory to itraconazole or caused by Scedosporium boydii responds to extended-spectrum oral voriconazole.

relationships.target: Primary Surgical Excision Alone Without Antifungal Coverage in Eumycetoma
relationships.keywords: surgical failure, local recurrence, unencapsulated resection, eumycetoma
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Fungal eumycetoma is resistant to surgical eradication alone; surgery without prolonged antifungal encapsulation results in rapid local recurrence and tissue dissemination.

relationships.target: Standard Antibacterial Therapy Administered for Fungal Eumycetoma
relationships.keywords: therapeutic failure, antibacterial mismatch, eumycetoma progression
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Fungal eumycetoma is intrinsically resistant to antibacterial regimens, leading to continuous clinical progression and limb loss.

relationships.target: Antifungal Azole Monotherapy Administered for Bacterial Actinomycetoma
relationships.keywords: therapeutic failure, antifungal mismatch, actinomycetoma progression
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Bacterial actinomycetoma is intrinsically resistant to antifungal azole therapy, which lacks antibacterial efficacy and results in complete treatment failure.
